title: Staged tenant evacuation, priming, and observed rollback playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: implement a deterministic, observable, and reversible data-plane upgrade flow for private (VPC) deployments that achieves zero-customer-downtime for steady-state traffic and provides fast, automated rollback when observed health regressions occur. Scope covers Terraform/IaC module conventions, pre-upgrade priming, staged tenant evacuation, health-driven canary promotion, automated rollback triggers, and post-rollback reconciliation. This ticket produces the playbook plus Terraform orchestration examples and an accompanying runbook snippet for on-call engineers. Success metrics: no more than one customer-facing error spike per major rollout (target 0), automated rollback within 5 minutes of SLO breach detection, and reproducible exercises in staging and 2 customer VPCs in Dedicated beta.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules provide a single 'apply' path that performs staged tenant slice updates with state-locking and idempotent plans
Synthetic priming phase that warms KV caches and model weights for each new instance before traffic cutover
Observable canary promotion policy: 1%, 10%, 50%, 100% by tenant-slice with automated health gating at each step
Automated rollback triggers based on multiple signals (p95 latency increase > 25%, error rate > 1% absolute, cache-miss spike > 40%, or abnormal error-budget burn)
Rollback completes within SLA (target: 5 minutes average from trigger to traffic reversion) and leaves system in a consistent state (no split-brain KV caches)
Playbook and runbook validated with a dry-run in staging and an on-call runbook drill with SRE and Solutions Eng participation
runbook_steps: 1) Lock target tenant slice via terraform state lock and create pre-upgrade snapshot of KV cache metadata to S3
2) Execute Terraform plan with 'staged_count=canary' parameter; provision new runtime instances in passive mode (no service traffic)
3) Trigger synthetic priming traffic to new instances for model weight load and KV warm-up until cache hit threshold met
4) Promote traffic in fractions: 1% -> wait 3m observe -> 10% -> wait 5m observe -> 50% -> wait 10m observe -> full
5) At each step, evaluate health checks (latency p95, 5xx rate, cache hit ratio, synthetic probe pass rate, customer error reports). If any metric crosses threshold, run automated rollback routine
6) Automated rollback: mark new instances out of service, re-route traffic to previous generation, run KV reconciliation to resynchronize caches, and tear down failed instances via terraform destroy
7) Post-rollback: attach incident ticket, collect diagnostics (heap profiles, logs, traces), create a remediation PR and rebase rollout approach before next attempt
